EnvoL 0.6.0: the compiler, built by itself, with the standard library and the `envo` tool. Apache-2.0.

**Download** `envol-0.6.0.tar` and unpack it anywhere (`tar -xf`, which Windows 10 and later also have). `bin/` holds `envo` and `envoc` for Linux and Windows (x86-64). Try `bin/envo hello.envol`. The library sits beside `bin/`, where `envo` finds it. [Getting started](https://github.com/envoscale/EnvoScale/blob/main/getting-started.md) has the rest.

**What's new**

- Apache-2.0: free for any use, including commercial.
- The language is EnvoL, in `.envol` files. Packages can depend on git repositories, pinned by commit.
- Faster generated code: the compiler lexes and parses its own sources in about a third of the time 0.5.0 took (arguments in registers, jump threading, inlining, unrolled small copies, folded addressing, loop-invariant loads).
- Examples that run as shown, checked in CI.
- The documentation for every project is in [EnvoScale](https://github.com/envoscale/EnvoScale).

**How it was built.** CI built this archive on Linux and on Windows from the same commit and published it only because both builds were byte-identical. The first compiler came from the `seed-2` release of [EnvoScaleAsm](https://github.com/envoscale/EnvoScaleAsm), built from assembly. `envol-0.6.0.provenance.json` records the commit, the command and the digests of the compilers; `SHA256SUMS` has the archive's digest.

**Not yet:** the archive is not signed, there are no macOS or AArch64 Linux builds of the tools themselves (programs for those targets do build: `--target aarch64-macos`, `--target aarch64-linux`), and everything is experimental: see the [status page](https://github.com/envoscale/EnvoScale/blob/main/project/status.md).
